0.2.0.lead: This is nexmix 0.2: beside Plex you now connect Jellyfin and Music Assistant too, and playlists move between the servers. What 0.1 had stays as it was.

sections.title: Jellyfin and Music Assistant
sections.body: Beside Plex, Jellyfin and Music Assistant join as media servers, several of one kind as well. Jellyfin is connected by Quick Connect or an API key, and you choose the user the playlists belong to there. For Music Assistant you enter a long-lived token of a user with full rights and choose the providers whose tracks count.

sections.title: One source per playlist
sections.body: When you make a playlist, you choose the server it takes its tracks from. Search, suggestions and listening in use that server's library, and the playlist lives there too, kept in step both ways as with Plex before. Guests only notice that the search uses that server.

sections.title: Copy and move
sections.body: “Copy to …” puts a playlist on another server as well. With “Keep in step” it stays a mirror there that follows its source; “Copy once” makes a new playlist of its own instead. “Move to …” makes the other server the source, and the old playlist stays as a mirror or is deleted there. A preview says first how many tracks were found. What is missing or unsure you match by hand or leave out.
sections.where: A playlist, Copy to … and Move to …

sections.title: Take everything over at once
sections.body: For a change of server, “Take all over …” brings every playlist of the other servers along, as mirrors or moved, with the same preview. It runs in the background and can let go of the old server afterwards without losing a playlist.
sections.where: Settings › Server, the card of the new server

sections.title: In step while you watch
sections.body: What changes in a playlist in Jellyfin or Music Assistant arrives in nexmix, from Music Assistant at once. A track added only in a mirror that has no sure match in the source is listed at the playlist as “only on …” until you decide.

sections.title: What Jellyfin and Music Assistant lack
sections.body: Neither knows moods or a sonic analysis. The mood filter and “Fill by mood” say so; genre and decade work. Music Assistant cannot move entries and takes them out by their place only. When somebody changes a playlist there right while nexmix writes it, a track may go missing, and the playlist says “Changed in Music Assistant at the same time”. Listening in on a track of Music Assistant plays the preview of another server with the same track, else its first 30 seconds.

small: Music Assistant needs a token of a user with full rights there, because nexmix must be able to cancel its own changes. The token lasts a year, and nexmix says so 30 days before.
“Ready for the internet?” checks Jellyfin and Music Assistant too.
The card of each server counts its playlists apart, as source and as mirror.
The interface under /api/v1 knows the servers, their mirrors, copying and moving.

0.1.0.lead: This is nexmix 0.1: build playlists together from your Plex library, with accounts of your own for the household and guests by a link. Every playlist is a playlist in Plex as well, and so in Plexamp. It is the first release, and it is still young.

sections.title: Playlists together
sections.body: A playlist belongs to the person who makes it. They share it with others to look at or to build along. Every track says who added it. What one person changes, everybody else sees at once, and what was taken out comes back with “Undo”. Deleted playlists stay in the trash for 30 days.

sections.title: Search the whole library
sections.body: nexmix fetches the catalogue from Plex once and then searches in the browser, without asking Plex while you type. A song stands there once, even when it is on the album, a best-of and a reissue. Filters by mood, decade and genre, and albums and artists with all their tracks.

sections.title: Suggestions and moods
sections.body: On the right nexmix suggests tracks that fit the last tracks of the list: from mood, style, genre and decade, from the other playlists of the household and, once Plex has finished its sonic analysis, by how they sound. “Fill by mood” puts a whole list together, and you tick what goes in.
sections.where: A playlist, right column and Fill by mood

sections.title: Listening in
sections.body: A click on ▶ plays 30 seconds from a good third into the track. The sound goes through nexmix, your Plex key stays on the server.

sections.title: In Plex, both ways
sections.body: The operator connects Plex by signing in at plex.tv. What happens in nexmix reaches Plex two seconds later. What is added, renamed or taken out in Plex or Plexamp arrives in nexmix, and the playlists Plex already has show up here. When both sides change at once, no track gets lost.

sections.title: Guests by a link
sections.body: For a party you invite guests with a link or a QR code. They only type their name, with no account and no app, and see only this one playlist. You decide whether they may add, sort and listen in, how many tracks each one brings, and how long the invitation lasts.

sections.title: Accounts and signing in
sections.body: Members get an invitation and an account of their own, with a password or through a sign-in provider such as authentik, Pocket ID or Microsoft Entra ID. A second factor and passkeys come with it. Nobody needs a Plex account but the operator.

small: Backups of the whole database, by hand or on a schedule, and restoring them in the same place.
Light and dark, on the phone as on the computer, in German and English. The operator uploads more languages.
An interface under /api/v1 for devices and programs, with keys that only read.
